title: Templates
summary: Every piece of text the system sends or prints, editable without touching code.
html:
Templates hold the wording of everything the system sends or prints: the email that goes with an invoice, the welcome message a new customer gets, the reminder for an overdue account, the layout of the printed quote.

Editing a template needs no programming. It is the single highest-value thing to do after installing, because the default wording is generic and your customers read it.

Finding the right one

Templates lists them all. The names are systematic: templates whose key starts email_template_ are emails, and the rest of the name says which one. So the email sent with an invoice is email_template_invoice, and so on.

If you are not sure which template produced a message, search the template list for a distinctive phrase from the message.

Variables

Templates contain placeholders that are replaced when the message is sent — the customer's name, the invoice number, the amount, a link to pay. Each template's edit screen lists the variables available to it, which is the list to work from; a variable that belongs to a different template is left as-is in the output, which is how {invoice_number} ends up printed literally in a welcome email.

Editing safely

Change the wording freely. Be careful with two things:

  • Do not delete a variable you did not mean to. Removing the payment link from the invoice email is easy to do and hard to notice.
  • Keep the links. Quote approval and invoice payment both depend on the link in the email.

Send yourself a test after editing. Every template that goes to a customer can be emailed to you first.

Print layouts

The printed quote and invoice are templates too. Small changes — wording, which fields appear — are made here. Anything structural is better done in the custom/ folder so it survives the next update; see Customising.
